title: Breakout EA results
author: Different-Team6219
selftext: The backtests results of the free EA ‘universal breakout’ (MT5) look very good netting on average 20%+ a year over the last 3 years with 9% max drawdown(60% a year with risk increased and only 5/6% increased drawdown). Just wondering if anyone has used it live and seen good results or if you have tweaked inputs or the strategy and seen better results? Or if anyone thinks the EA has been optimised to a certain time frame corrupting backtests?

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body:
I haven't used this EA, so I can't speak to live results, but the numbers you quote raise a few questions. Raising risk to get 60% a year while max drawdown only rises by 5 or 6 points is odd. Drawdown normally scales roughly in proportion to risk, so a threefold return for a small drawdown increase suggests the backtest isn't behaving like real trading. It could be the way the tester sequences trades, a hidden martingale or grid component, or very few trades, so I'd check the trade count and the worst losing streak before trusting any of it.

For the "optimised to a timeframe" question, a quick test is to change the inputs slightly (periods, breakout distance, stop size) and see if results fall apart. A real edge survives small changes, and a fitted one usually doesn't. Then test it on older years it wasn't tuned on, and on other symbols.

Check the testing setup too: "every tick based on real ticks," realistic spread and commission, and slippage on stops. Breakout systems are especially sensitive to those, because entries happen when spreads widen. They're also exposed around scheduled news like NFP, CPI and FOMC, so I'd see how much of the profit and drawdown falls near releases. Cymetica's EventTrader has pre-tagged event timing for that, or you can use any calendar.

Before any live money, run it on demo for a couple of months and compare fills to the backtest.

How many trades are in the three years of tests?
